provenance: LLM-backend-derived + deterministic-checked (Phase 16/17 inverted boundary) — NOT a ship typology config. GLUED-NO-SEPARATOR: markitdown dropped this advisory's bullet glyphs AND blank-line separators, so the red-flag paragraphs fuse into a few blocks (the rf_region block counter sizes them as ~6, not the 24 genuine flags); the deterministic extractor was deleted in Phase 17. The LLM backend read the source and EXTRACTED all 24 red flags directly; the deterministic gate GROUNDS each verbatim `flag` in the source md within the red-flag region + checks the cover×data matrix — reaching a glued advisory the structural parser never could, with no post-hoc splitter and no new converter. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo).

indicators.flag: A customer with neither legal permanent residence in the United States nor significant experience in the health care industry (e.g., based on the customer's stated occupation) tries to open a bank account as the owner or employee of a recently established or purchased health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program.
indicators.red_flag: Account opening by an owner or employee of a newly established or purchased health care provider who has no US permanent residence and no health care industry experience
indicators.rationale: Onboarding KYC carries residency and stated occupation, but tying them to a freshly registered Health Care Benefit Program provider needs an entity-age + provider-registry enrichment we hold only partially; enrich, then build the new-provider onboarding screen.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program that has beneficial owners with prior health care or government benefits fraud convictions.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider whose beneficial owners have prior health care or government benefits fraud convictions
indicators.rationale: Prior fraud-conviction records on beneficial owners are not data a financial institution holds; source a criminal-history / debarment feed before any detection signal can exist.

indicators.flag: A customer is the nominal or beneficial owner of a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program and has familial or business affiliations with individuals with health care or government benefits fraud convictions.
indicators.red_flag: Nominal or beneficial owner of a health care provider with familial or business ties to individuals convicted of health care or government benefits fraud
indicators.rationale: Familial / business affiliation to convicted individuals needs both a relationship graph and conviction records we do not hold; source those feeds before building.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program, and the account is accessed through an Internet Protocol (IP) address or Device ID that is linked to multiple accounts at the financial institution or other financial institutions or connected to foreign jurisdictions.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider account accessed via an IP address or Device ID shared across multiple accounts or linked to foreign jurisdictions
indicators.rationale: Device/IP linkage analytics already exist for fraud-ring detection; enhance the existing screen with a health-care-provider + shared-device/foreign-IP conjunction rather than building net-new.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program and has nominal and beneficial owners listed on the account who also appear on bank accounts for other separate and distinct health care providers or suppliers.
indicators.red_flag: Nominal or beneficial owners of a health care provider account who also appear on accounts of other separate and distinct health care providers
indicators.rationale: Detecting shared owners across distinct provider accounts needs a beneficial-owner graph spanning accounts that we hold only partially; enrich the ownership graph, then build the shared-owner ring signal.

indicators.flag: A customer is a recently established or purchased health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program, and there are changes in the individuals listed as beneficiaries of the corporate account without a change to the name or Tax Identification Number on the account.
indicators.red_flag: Changes to the individuals listed as beneficiaries of a health care provider's corporate account with no change to the account name or Tax Identification Number
indicators.rationale: Beneficiary changes with a static name/TIN need a historized signatory/beneficiary record we keep only partially; enrich with beneficiary-change history, then build.

indicators.flag: A customer that is a recently established or purchased health care provider or supplier receives a significant amount of reimbursements from a Health Care Benefit Program or commercial insurers and then immediately transfers those funds to other recently established companies with the same nominal or beneficial owners, little to no online presence, and other indicators of illicit shell company activity.
indicators.red_flag: Reimbursements received by a newly established health care provider and immediately passed to other newly established same-owner companies showing shell company indicators
indicators.rationale: Reimbursements landing and immediately passing to same-owner newly-formed companies is an uncovered shell pass-through, and inbound reimbursement flow, counterparty entity age, and beneficial-owner overlap are all in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a recently established health care provider receives a significant reimbursement from a Health Care Benefit Program or commercial insurer and shortly afterward transfers an equivalent amount to other recently established companies sharing its nominal or beneficial owners — a same-owner shell pass-through of program funds
build_logic.source: Core transaction + counterparty features (Gold); beneficial-owner overlap; counterparty entity-age registry
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a recently established health care provider or supplier that receives a significant number of reimbursements from a Health Care Benefit Program or commercial insurers soon after starting operations.
indicators.red_flag: Newly established health care provider receiving a significant number of program or insurer reimbursements soon after starting operations
indicators.rationale: A brand-new provider drawing heavy reimbursements right after opening is uncovered, and entity age (account-open date) plus reimbursement volume are both in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a health care provider account opened recently receives a significant number and value of Health Care Benefit Program or insurer reimbursements within a short window of starting operations — early-life reimbursement volume well above the peer-provider baseline
build_logic.source: Core reimbursement transaction + account-open features (Gold); MAC/insurer payer tagging
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program that is receiving a significant increase in reimbursements soon after a change in beneficial ownership.
indicators.red_flag: Significant increase in a health care provider's reimbursements soon after a change in beneficial ownership
indicators.rationale: Reimbursement-surge monitoring exists; enhance it to key on the conjunction with a recent beneficial-ownership change rather than standing up a separate rule.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that suddenly has a significant increase in reimbursements from Health Care Benefit Programs or commercial insurers.
indicators.red_flag: Sudden significant increase in a health care provider's reimbursements from programs or commercial insurers
indicators.rationale: A sudden step-change in reimbursement volume against a provider's own baseline is uncovered and computable directly from the reimbursement time series in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a health care provider's monthly reimbursement value from Health Care Benefit Programs or insurers jumps sharply above its own trailing baseline — a sudden surge ratio beyond the provider's established norm
build_logic.source: Core reimbursement transaction features (Gold); MAC/insurer payer tagging
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a recently established or purchased health care provider or supplier registered with Health Care Benefit Programs or commercial insurers that receives a significant amount of reimbursements inconsistent with the customer's profile (e.g., receiving a significant amount of payments from Medicare Part A and Part B MACs for reimbursements beyond the expected activity of other similar health care providers or suppliers).
indicators.red_flag: Newly established health care provider receiving reimbursements inconsistent with its profile and beyond the expected activity of similar providers
indicators.rationale: Profile/peer-deviation scoring already exists for transaction monitoring; enhance it with a provider-peer reimbursement benchmark rather than building net-new.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that receives significant volumes of reimbursements from a Health Care Benefit Program or commercial insurers but has little to no legitimate business expenses associated with the provision of health care goods and services (e.g., receiving reimbursements from DME MACs but little to no purchases of DME).
indicators.red_flag: Significant reimbursement inflows to a health care provider with little to no legitimate business expenses for providing health care goods and services
indicators.rationale: High inbound reimbursements with near-zero matching operating outflows (supplies, payroll, DME purchases) is an uncovered no-opex shell pattern, and inbound vs categorized-outbound flow is in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a health care provider receives significant reimbursement inflows but shows little to no legitimate operating outflow over the same period — operating-expense-to-reimbursement ratio near zero with no supply purchases or payroll, inconsistent with genuine provision of health care goods and services
build_logic.source: Core transaction features with merchant/category tagging (Gold); reimbursement payer tagging
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that receives a significant volume of reimbursements from a single Health Care Benefit Program as opposed to other customers that receive reimbursements from multiple Health Care Benefit Programs (e.g., a customer is receiving a significant amount of reimbursements from one MAC for only one type of health care good or service such as DME).
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider drawing a significant reimbursement volume from a single program, unlike peers who draw from multiple programs
indicators.rationale: Payer concentration is computable from reimbursement source tagging already monitored for other purposes; enhance with a single-program / single-service concentration score versus peers.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier with a significant amount of transactional activity consisting of "consulting fees," "marketing fees," and other nondescriptive, repetitive invoices.
indicators.red_flag: Significant transactional activity labeled as consulting fees, marketing fees, and other nondescriptive, repetitive invoices
indicators.rationale: Flagging nondescriptive repetitive memo lines (consulting/marketing fees) needs transaction-memo text we capture only partially as structured data; enrich with memo NLP, then build the invoice-pattern signal.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that receives a significant volume of reimbursements from a Health Care Benefit Program and transfers the funds to another company registered to a residential address.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider receiving significant program reimbursements and transferring the funds to a company registered to a residential address
indicators.rationale: Detecting a counterparty registered to a residential address needs an address-type / business-registry enrichment we hold only partially; enrich, then build the program-funds-to-residential-entity signal.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that has outgoing transactions to, or expenditures related to, companies that have no apparent related nexus to the health care industry. This could include residential real estate and luxury goods such as art or jewelry.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider outflows to companies with no apparent nexus to health care, such as residential real estate and luxury goods like art or jewelry
indicators.rationale: Merchant-category and luxury-spend tagging partially exist; enhance the existing high-risk-spend screen with a health-care-provider + no-industry-nexus outflow conjunction.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier with consistently low to moderate billing for a year or more and then suddenly begins to file a large number of claims (i.e., spike billing).
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider with a year or more of consistently low to moderate billing that suddenly files a large number of claims (spike billing)
indicators.rationale: A long low-billing baseline followed by an abrupt claims spike is an uncovered dormant-then-spike pattern, and the per-provider reimbursement/claims time series in repo makes it immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a health care provider sustains consistently low to moderate billing for a year or more, then abruptly files a large volume of claims — a spike ratio far above a long quiet baseline (dormant-then-spike billing)
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier with a pattern of making significant cash withdrawals for no readily apparent business reason.
indicators.red_flag: Pattern of significant cash withdrawals by a health care provider with no readily apparent business reason
indicators.rationale: Significant unexplained cash withdrawals are already captured by the institution's standing cash-activity monitoring; no new build needed.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier with a significant increase in cash withdrawals correlating to a significant increase in billings (i.e., customer is potentially paying kickbacks).
indicators.red_flag: Significant increase in a health care provider's cash withdrawals correlating with a significant increase in billings (potential kickback payments)
indicators.rationale: The correlation of rising cash withdrawals with rising billings (a kickback signature) is uncovered, and both cash-withdrawal and reimbursement time series are in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a health care provider's cash withdrawals rise in step with its billings over time — a positive correlation between increasing cash-out and increasing reimbursements, consistent with billings funding kickback cash payments
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → health-care fraud review gate

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier that is transferring a significant volume of funds to individuals via high-value checks.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider transferring a significant volume of funds to individuals via high-value checks
indicators.rationale: High-value check monitoring exists; enhance it to surface a provider transferring significant check volume to individual payees specifically.

indicators.flag: Without credible explanation, a customer routinely cashes high-value checks drawn from accounts associated with a health care provider or supplier.
indicators.red_flag: Customer routinely cashing high-value checks drawn on health care provider accounts without credible explanation
indicators.rationale: Routine cashing of high-value checks is already within the institution's standing check / cash monitoring; no new build needed.

indicators.flag: A customer that is a health care provider or supplier, or the customer's employee, engages in behavior suggesting efforts to evade the Currency Transaction Report (CTR) reporting requirement (e.g., alters or cancels a transaction when advised a CTR would be filed or engages in structuring with multiple cash transactions for under $10,000), as well as avoid recordkeeping requirements.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider or its employee acting to evade CTR reporting and recordkeeping, e.g. altering or cancelling a transaction when told a CTR would file, or structuring under $10,000
indicators.rationale: CTR-evasion / structuring detection is a mature, already-deployed BSA control; no new build needed for this typology.

indicators.flag: A customer is a recently established or purchased health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program that sends a significant amount of wire transfers to individuals and companies located in foreign jurisdictions.
indicators.red_flag: Newly established health care provider sending a significant amount of wire transfers to individuals and companies in foreign jurisdictions
indicators.rationale: Cross-border wire monitoring exists; enhance it with a new-provider + significant-foreign-wire conjunction rather than a standalone rule.

indicators.flag: A customer is a health care provider or supplier registered with a Health Care Benefit Program that sends money transfers to VASPs, brokerage accounts, and online betting platforms for no seemingly legitimate business reason.
indicators.red_flag: Health care provider sending money transfers to VASPs, brokerage accounts, and online betting platforms with no seemingly legitimate business reason
indicators.rationale: Flagging transfers to VASPs / brokerages / betting platforms needs counterparty-type tagging of those destinations we hold only partially; enrich the counterparty registry, then build the out-of-pattern-destination signal.
